items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the incorporation of the inorganic gas of the air into an organic compound”
o: Photorespiration
Calvin cycle
PEP carboxylase
Carbon fixation
items.s: Carbon fixation is the incorporation of the inorganic gas of the air into an organic compound.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Controlled atmosphere storage?
o: a species adapted to complete its life cycle in strongly salty surroundings
the holding of produce under a deliberately adjusted mixture of gases to slow its metabolism
the adjustment of an individual so that it tolerates a condition it could not previously endure
the adjustment of solute content to hold moisture and keep the living contents intact
items.s: Controlled atmosphere storage: the holding of produce under a deliberately adjusted mixture of gases to slow its metabolism. The other options describe Acclimation, Osmoregulation, Halophyte.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the series of carriers that pass reducing equivalents to a final acceptor while pumping protons”
o: Substrate level phosphorylation
Electron transport chain
Respiratory quotient
Krebs cycle
items.s: Electron transport chain is the series of carriers that pass reducing equivalents to a final acceptor while pumping protons.

items.q: In this course, Transpiration refers to
o: the exudation of droplets from leaf tips through special openings at night
the explanation of upward movement in the conducting strands by pull transmitted through a continuous column
the loss of vapour from the aerial surfaces of a plant
the breaking of a continuous column by an air bubble that refills a conducting element
items.s: Transpiration: the loss of vapour from the aerial surfaces of a plant. The other options describe Cavitation, Guttation, Cohesion tension theory.

items.q: “the generation of energy-rich phosphate bonds using the proton gradient built by the flow of reducing equivalents” is the definition of
o: Glycolysis
Krebs cycle
Electron transport chain
Oxidative phosphorylation
items.s: Oxidative phosphorylation is the generation of energy-rich phosphate bonds using the proton gradient built by the flow of reducing equivalents.

items.q: The correct meaning of Cavitation is
o: one of the pair of specialised epidermal bodies whose shape change opens or closes a pore
the breaking of a continuous column by an air bubble that refills a conducting element
the loss of vapour from the aerial surfaces of a plant
the rate at which vapour can pass out through a pore in the surface layer
items.s: Cavitation: the breaking of a continuous column by an air bubble that refills a conducting element. The other options describe Transpiration, Guard cell, Stomatal conductance.

items.q: The correct meaning of Photorespiration is
o: the wasteful uptake of oxygen by the sugar-building enzyme that releases previously captured carbon
the sequence of reactions that builds sugar from the gas of the air using chemical energy and reducing power
the incorporation of the inorganic gas of the air into an organic compound
one of the layer of bodies surrounding the conducting strand in a leaf of many grasses
items.s: Photorespiration: the wasteful uptake of oxygen by the sugar-building enzyme that releases previously captured carbon. The other options describe Bundle sheath cell, Calvin cycle, Carbon fixation.

items.q: Geotropism may be defined as
o: the control of development by the relative length of the light and dark phases
a species that begins flowering only when the dark period is shorter than a certain length, as wheat does
the growth response of a part along the line of gravity
a species that begins flowering only when the unbroken dark period exceeds a certain length, as chrysanthemum does
items.s: Geotropism: the growth response of a part along the line of gravity. The other options describe Photoperiodism, Short day plant, Long day plant.

items.q: Phytochrome may be defined as
o: the promotion of flowering by exposure to a period of low temperature
the bending of a growing part towards or away from a directional source of radiation
the control of development by the relative length of the light and dark phases
the compound that interconverts between two forms on absorbing red and far red wavelengths
items.s: Phytochrome: the compound that interconverts between two forms on absorbing red and far red wavelengths. The other options describe Phototropism, Vernalisation, Photoperiodism.
